$comment: The mapping set for the Sheffield PGT form, DRAFT, one file for the whole blueprint (a plan reads one set).
Authored from Vahid's words; the approver is Iman Behravan (step 5 reviewer pair). Not usable until reviewed
by a second person, and not executable until every required field is mapped.
Equal opportunities (page9), 2026-09-11, ADR-0102 and Vahid's correction from the live dropdown: both values
are 'Prefer not to say'. The disability refusal COVERS the eleven other controls of the same question. The
ethnic-origin refusal quotes nothing: the field's captured text says nothing about a later opportunity.
Personal (page3) and contact (page4), P89: mapped as far as the profile registry reaches. Date of birth is
three selects, rendered with the D / MMMM / YYYY patterns. The e-mail is asked twice and mapped twice. The
country select takes the portal's own upper-case names; the option map here is PARTIAL — eight countries
whose names the capture shows — and a student from any other refuses to render (render_refused) rather
than being approximated. The reviewer extends it from the captured option list, never from memory.
NOT mapped, and why: employment (page8) asks four required fields — start date, position, employer,
duties — for which the profile registry has no field. A registry addition is a product decision (what the
profile collects), raised in P89, not made here. Every optional field without a mapping is passed over.
Registration (page0), P91, from the signed-out read of the entry page: the e-mail from the profile; the two
password fields as secure_credential for portal_account_creation, filled by the Secure Plane from a value
nothing else holds, which checkUsable requires of any password field (ADR-0043).

Education (page7), P98: the page repeats over education.prior_qualifications (ADR-0104). Its six document slots are student handoffs — the student attaches them, and the preview says so under each qualification. No field on it is mapped yet: the registry's Qualification has level, subject, institution, countryCode, completionYear, grade and gradeScale, and which portal box each fills waits on the reviewer.

P100 (ADR-0105): the six status radios beside the education page's slots are handed to the student with their slots — 'My transcript is in English' is the student answering the question the slot asks. The subject list is loaded by pressing subjectSearchButton after typing subjectSearch (the dependencies read names the control: onclick searchSubjects()); the press is recorded on the field, not mapped.

Education (page7), ADR-0107 (2026-09-12): the six status radios are no longer handed to the student — a companion is mapped by nothing. When the radio's option values are read from a copy of the fieldset markup, the blueprint names each slot's defer option (whenDeferred) and its 'not providing' option (whenNotProviding); until then the slots are the student's act on a page nothing fills, which is admitted.

Education (page7), P108 (2026-09-12): the six Documentary Evidence radios' values are now in the blueprint (0.2.12) from Vahid's reading of the live page — whenAttached Uploaded, whenDeferred UploadLater, whenNotProviding NotSending on every slot; NotRequired is the fourth value and is named by nothing. With the defer value named, the page is NO LONGER one that nothing fills: each qualification's six radios are set to UploadLater by the runner while the qualification's own fields (institution, degree, subject, dates, grade) still wait on the reviewer. DO NOT SIGN this set while that is so — a run would save a qualification that says only 'later' six times. The certificate slot's companion is paired with certificateStatus from the file input's own handler (onchange ticks certificateUploadRadio, the id of that group's Uploaded option), not from the name; the radio's copy says 'proof of registration', so what the slot IS is Iman's to settle from the page (README, P108).

Language (page6), P109 (2026-09-12): the certificate group's values are in the blueprint (0.2.13) from Vahid's live reading — Uploaded / UploadLater / NotSending / NotRequired, the same shape as education — and its companion names the three; previousEnglishEducation submits Yes / No. Nothing on this page is mapped, so its companion is left as the form has it. NotRequired here reads 'We do not require a certificate to be uploaded if you are a UK appl[icant]…' — a claim about who the applicant is: the third distinct meaning of that one token on this form, and never ours to choose. Twenty-three radio groups on personal, contact and nationality still carry the capture's element ids as values; no mapping names one, and none may until each page is read the same way.

Personal, contact, nationality (pages 3-5), P110 (2026-09-12): every radio group's values are now in the blueprint (0.2.14) from Vahid's reading with the snippet. The yes-or-no groups do NOT agree on case across the form — personal.do submits Yes / No, nationality.do yes / no — so a constant on one must carry that page's case exactly; the runner sets a radio by value and normalises nothing. corrContactDateType: the value 'After' is shown as 'From this date:' and 'Before' as 'To this date:' — map from the text beside the value, never from the value alone. The five nationality document slots still carry no companion: their groups' values are known (Uploaded / UploadLater / NotSending, no NotRequired) but the slot-to-group pairing waits on the file inputs' own handler markup, which Vahid offered to read.

Nationality (page5), P111 (2026-09-13): each of the five file inputs carries onchange: document.getElementById('<slot>UploadRadio').checked=true, and no radio on the page carried such an id when Vahid read it. The handler names the intent; the DOM as read does not show which group the id belongs to, and if it belongs to nothing the handler throws and the page ticks nothing on attach. The five companions stay out of the blueprint until one more reading settles which (README, P111). When they go in, the runner needs only the group's name and the value Uploaded — both read — not the id.

Nationality (page5), P112 (2026-09-13): the five document slots are NOT on an international student's path. showHideDocumentUploads(), read by Vahid from the live page, shows each upload only on a claim of UK status — a British passport, indefinite leave, marriage to a UK citizen, refugee status — and with nationality and residence set to Iran none appeared. The blueprint (0.2.15) carries visibleWhen on four of the five file inputs from the function's own reads (yes on britishPassport / indefinateVisa / spouseOfUKCitizen / refugeeStatus); utilityBillScan is shown on britishPassport OR indefinateVisa, which the condition vocabulary cannot say, so it carries none and the plan treats it as an optional unmapped field, passed over. No slot on this page is to be mapped for an international student; a document mapped to one would be attached into a hidden block. The five companions are moot for the path and stay out.

Education (page7), P113 (2026-09-13): the repeating page's listing is named (ADR-0106) from Vahid's read of summary.do with two qualifications saved — each entry's heading is an h5 reading exactly 'Previous Education N' inside div.homepageInfomation (misspelled on the page; kept as written) inside div.homepageBlock, both wrappers shared by every section. The entry locator is text-shaped by necessity — the structure counts sections — and exact to the number: h5:text-matches('^Previous Education [0-9]+$'). A qualification is saved when that count grows by one.

Contact (page4), P116 (2026-09-13): the UK postcode is two boxes — corrPostcode and corrPostcode2 both came back from Vahid's read-back, three characters each for his — so the single-value mapping was wrong and is replaced by the uk_postcode format on each box, split at the postcode's own seam (inward = last three, outward = the rest), never at 3+3. Nothing on this page was normalised by the portal: e-mail, address, town and postcode came back exactly as typed, case included. The permanent-address fields (perm*) stay unmapped, as before.

mappings.note: The address the account is registered under; the same one the contact page asks for again.
Chosen by the student in the secure box (ADR-0042); never a value here.
The same password, typed again by the Secure Plane.
First / Given Name:* — the captured label carries the asterisk.
Family Name:* — the captured label carries the asterisk.
Date of Birth:* asked as three selects; the day options are '1'…'31', unpadded.
The month options are English names, 'January'…'December'.
The year options are four-digit years.
E-mail:* — the address the account was registered with; the reviewer confirms the portal accepts a different one here.
Confirm E-Mail:* — the same value typed again, as the form asks.
Country:* — the portal's own upper-case names as values. PARTIAL map; any other country refuses to render, for the reviewer to extend from the captured options.

UK Post Code: (* UK only) — the FIRST of two boxes (maxlength 4), shown when the country is the United Kingdom. The outward code, split at the postcode's own seam (P116: Vahid's read-back showed two boxes, and 'must not assume 3+3'). The portal stores it as typed, case included.
The SECOND UK postcode box (maxlength 4): the inward code — a digit and two letters, always three characters. Hidden with the first when the country is not the United Kingdom.

The international postcode box, shown when the country is not the United Kingdom. Both boxes carry the same part; the plan honours the blueprint's visibleWhen (P90), so only the box the form shows is filled.

source.rationale: Health is Article 9 data this system does not hold. The form's own 'Prefer not to say' is ticked: a stated refusal to route the answer through AskiMate, not the student's answer. The empty save is refused (Vahid, 2026-09-11), so a refusal the form offers is the only honest entry.
source.formSays: if you go on to register on a course you will have another opportunity to answer later

mappings.note: Vahid, 2026-09-11: 'the "Prefer not to say" checkbox, whose own label reads "if you go on to register on a course you will have another opportunity to answer later". That line is the form's words and may be quoted.'

source.rationale: Ethnic origin is Article 9 data this system does not hold. The form's own 'Prefer not to say' option (998) is selected: a stated refusal, not the student's answer.

mappings.note: Vahid, 2026-09-11, from the live dropdown: 'the option is "Prefer not to say". There is no "Information withheld" entry in the list.' The field's captured text carries no later-opportunity statement, so nothing is quoted.
